title: Snowflake Cortex Review: Pricing, Limits and the Open Source Alternative (2026)
summary: Snowflake Cortex Analyst and Snowflake Intelligence (now CoWork) reviewed: how they work, pricing, limits, and nao, the open source alternative on Snowflake.
body_markdown:
Snowflake Cortex answers questions on Snowflake data, and only on Snowflake data.


**Snowflake Cortex** is Snowflake's AI suite. For analytics, it means **Cortex Analyst** (text-to-SQL over a semantic view), **Cortex Agents** (the agent runtime) and **Snowflake Intelligence** , now called **Snowflake CoWork** (the chat app for business users). It stops at the edge of Snowflake: your semantics live in Snowflake semantic views, every user needs a Snowflake role, and your agent's context stays inside Snowflake. **nao** is the open source alternative: an analytics agent your data team builds and controls, on Snowflake or any other warehouse, with its context in files you own.


This review comes from our hands-on[benchmark of 20 analytics agents](https://getnao.io/blog/ai-data-agents-compared/) and from Snowflake's docs.


## What is Snowflake Cortex?


Snowflake's agent stack has four parts, as Elementum[summarized this week](https://www.elementum.ai/blog/snowflake-agentic-ai) :


- **Cortex Agents** : the managed runtime. An agent is a schema-level object that bundles a model, tools and instructions. Generally available since November 4, 2025.
- **Snowflake CoWork** (formerly Snowflake Intelligence): the conversational app for business users, running on the Cortex Agent API. The old[Snowflake Intelligence docs page](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/snowflake-intelligence) now opens the CoWork overview.
- **Cortex Analyst** : generates SQL from natural language over a **semantic view** .
- **Cortex Search** : hybrid vector and keyword search over unstructured data.


The[Cortex Analyst docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst) now recommend moving to Cortex Agents, which support every Cortex Analyst capability. In practice, "Snowflake Cortex" for analytics is a Cortex Agent with Cortex Analyst as one of its tools, served through CoWork.


**Semantic views are Snowflake's semantic layer.** According to the[semantic views docs](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/views-semantic/overview) , they are schema-level objects holding logical tables, relationships, facts, metrics and dimensions, created from a YAML spec or imported from Tableau and Power BI files. The page does not mention dbt.


Cortex Analyst also has[evaluations](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/snowflake-cortex/cortex-analyst-evaluations) : they test one semantic view against its own verified queries and track accuracy, regressions and latency. The test set is written by hand, one semantic view per run.


## How much does Snowflake Cortex cost?


Cortex Analyst is billed **per successful message** , and the **warehouse that runs the generated SQL is billed separately** in Snowflake credits. No amounts here: they change, check Snowflake's consumption table.


So the real question is not the price of one answer. It is how much warehouse compute your users generate once the whole company asks questions, and whether you can leave if the price changes.


## Snowflake Cortex limitations


Teams look for a Snowflake Cortex alternative for four reasons:


1. **Snowflake only.** Cortex answers on data in Snowflake. Data in Postgres, BigQuery or Databricks stays invisible to it.
2. **Limited context.** The agent knows what fits in your semantic views and instructions. Your dbt docs, business rules and team knowledge stay outside unless you copy them in. In our benchmark we found no dbt integration in Cortex.
3. **Users need Snowflake identities.** The agent runs under the calling user's Snowflake role, which is good for governance but means every business user needs a Snowflake identity, the CORTEX_USER or CORTEX_ANALYST_USER database role, and SELECT on the tables.
4. **Getting it where people work is on you.** Alex Ross[wrote this week](https://cloudydata.substack.com/p/embedding-snowflake-cortex-agents) that people who build a Cortex Agent keep hearing the same request: can we use it in Teams, because most users never open Snowsight. His answer is an unofficial open source Teams app from Snowflake Labs.


## Should you build your analytics agent on Snowflake Cortex?


No, not if you want to keep control of it. An analytics agent is only as good as its context: the definitions, rules and examples your data team writes over months. Build it inside Cortex and that context lives in Snowflake's format, in Snowflake's interface:


- **Vendor lock-in.** Your context is tied to Snowflake semantic views. Moving warehouses, or adding one, means rebuilding the agent.
- **Your costs follow Snowflake pricing.** Messages and compute are billed in Snowflake credits, at Snowflake's rates.
- **Your agent's ceiling is Snowflake's roadmap.** If Cortex doesn't read your dbt project or support a new kind of context, you wait.


Keep the warehouse and the agent separate. With nao, the context is plain files in your own git repo: readable, versioned, reviewed like code, and portable. Switching or adding a warehouse is a config change, not a rebuild.


## nao: the open source alternative to Snowflake Cortex


**nao is open source (Apache 2.0).** You can read every line of the agent, self-host it on your own infrastructure or run it on nao Cloud, and bring the LLM of your choice. You don't pay before you see value.


Snowflake Cortex nao


License Proprietary, part of Snowflake **Open source, Apache 2.0**


Where it runs In your Snowflake account Self-hosted or nao Cloud


Warehouses Snowflake only Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, Postgres, Redshift, Athena, DuckDB, MotherDuck and more


Context Semantic views and instructions Files in your repo: schemas, previews, profiling, dbt docs,` RULES.md` , semantic layer, skills


Semantic layer Snowflake semantic views dbt MetricFlow, and your Snowflake semantic views synced as context


Evaluation Per semantic view, on verified queries` nao test` on your own questions, across models


Who can ask Users with a Snowflake role Anyone you invite, in nao Chat, Slack, Teams or Claude


LLM Run by Snowflake Yours: Claude, GPT, Gemini, Mistral, Bedrock, Ollama...


**You don't lose the work you did for Cortex.**` nao sync` reads the semantic views in your Snowflake schemas and writes each one into the agent's context, next to your dbt project and rules.


### How to build an analytics agent on Snowflake with nao


1. ` pip install nao-core` , then` nao init` and pick Snowflake ([database docs](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/databases) ).
2. ` nao sync` writes your Snowflake metadata as files. **Existing semantic views are synced too** : each one lands in the context as a` definition.md` with its DDL.
3. Add your[dbt repo](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/repos) and, if you use MetricFlow, point nao at your[dbt semantic layer](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-builder/semantic-layer) so metrics are compiled, not re-derived.
4. Write the business rules in` RULES.md` . Our[context engineering guide](https://getnao.io/blog/how-to-do-context-engineering-for-data-teams/) covers the method.
5. Write 20-40 real questions with their SQL and run[nao test](https://docs.getnao.io/nao-agent/context-engineering/evaluation) after every change, in CI if you want. A test passes only when the agent's data matches your SQL.
6. Deploy nao Chat, or plug it into[Slack](https://getnao.io/blog/setup-ai-analytics-slack-bot-open-source/) ,[Teams](https://getnao.io/blog/setup-ai-analytics-teams-bot-open-source/) or Claude through the[nao MCP](https://getnao.io/blog/launching-nao-mcp/) .


That is how our own agent went[from 45% to 86% reliability](https://getnao.io/blog/improve-analytics-agent-reliability-steps/) . For the side-by-side from our benchmark, see[nao vs Snowflake Cortex](https://getnao.io/resources/compare/snowflake-cortex/) .
